_podcast.theme_scoring_prompt: Rate how well this article fits the theme 'Cariboo Voices & Local News' — stories FROM and ABOUT the Cariboo-Chilcotin region and its communities. Score 80-100 for articles directly covering: news and events in Williams Lake, Quesnel, 100 Mile House, Bella Coola, Horsefly, Likely, Anahim Lake, Alexis Creek, or the Cariboo Regional District; local government and civic decisions (City of Williams Lake, City of Quesnel, CRD, District of 100 Mile House); local health services and emergency closures; local economy, businesses, and community programs; Cariboo arts, culture, and community events; AND digital equity, rural internet access (fiber, fixed wireless, Starlink), and connectivity serving these specific communities. Articles from local Cariboo news sources (mycariboonow.com, wltribune.com, quesnelobserver.com, 100milefreepress.net, cfjctoday.com) covering Cariboo community life should score 65-85. Score 50-79 for: BC provincial news directly affecting Cariboo communities, rural Canadian community stories closely paralleling Cariboo life, digital equity and rural internet broadly. Score 20-49 for: general BC news that may affect rural areas, broader rural Canada topics without specific Cariboo tie-in. Score 0-19 for: national/international news without Cariboo relevance, pure tech or entertainment with no community angle. Penalise heavily (score 0–20): international geopolitical and war news with no Cariboo tie-in; science discoveries without a local community connection; consumer tech reviews and gadget guides; wildlife and conservation stories not involving Cariboo communities or First Nations; BC provincial news without direct Cariboo-region relevance. Score 0-100 where 100 is a perfect thematic match and 0 is completely unrelated.

items.title: [cbc.ca] Quebec separatist Parti Québécois wins minority government, reviving referendum drive
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

The Parti Québécois won 59 of 127 seats in Quebec’s Oct. 5 election, returning to power under leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon but falling five seats short of the 64 needed for a majority. The Liberals won 40 seats, the Conservatives 19 and Québec solidaire nine. The Coalition Avenir Québec, which had governed for eight years, won none. The PQ received about 28% of the vote [castanet.net#1][cbc.ca#1][lapresse.ca#1]. St-Pierre Plamondon reiterated his call for a referendum on Quebec sovereignty but said he would wait until U.S. President Donald Trump’s term ends in 2029. As a minority government, the PQ will need opposition support to pass legislation and survive confidence votes. St-Pierre Plamondon said voters had asked the party to work with other parties [wral.com#1][cbc.ca#2][bbc.co.uk#1][dw.com#1]. The PQ’s platform includes cutting government spending by $6.6 billion over five years, reducing immigration and changing health-care administration. Prime Minister Mark Carney congratulated St-Pierre Plamondon and said building a stronger Quebec is central to building a stronger Canada [cbc.ca#2][perthnow.com.au#1].

items.content_html:

If so, the first animals may have lived before or during Snowball Earth, leaving behind little trace because their soft bodies were rarely preserved.

items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] ‘I do not know if the doctor survived’: young mothers recall ‘living hell’ of Nepal’s floods
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Kalpana Nepali was seven months pregnant when the flash floods hit last month, while Pooja Pariyal spent three days on a hospital roof waiting to be rescued. Now, they are living precariously in temporary shelters

For three days, Pooja Pariyal waited on the roof of Trishuli hospital with her three-month-old daughter, Ridhika. On the ground below and around the building, most of her town had been destroyed and churned into a sea of mud in the catastrophic flash floods that surged through the Himayalan border region of Nepal and Tibet in August.

“Those three days were living hell for me, with no food, no working toilet and no one to help with the baby,” she says. “I had nothing to clean my baby’s soiled clothes. My milk supply had reduced because I was hungry and this poor little thing would cry her lungs out.

items.title: [ScienceDaily] Creatine may help build muscle even without exercise, researchers find
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

Creatine helped middle-aged adults gain muscle and strength even without a structured workout program in a new 12-week study. When combined with exercise and a calorie-reduced diet, it produced even greater strength gains while helping participants add lean tissue and lose fat. Researchers say the results strengthen the case for creatine as a potentially useful tool for maintaining muscle with age.

items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] ‘They take our water, our soil’: protesters fight ‘foreignisation’ as Javier Milei encourages land sales in Argentina
items.content_html:
🏔️ ✏️

The country’s far-right president is courting billionaire investors by removing a block on foreign ownership of land and natural resources

On 19 September, Marta Sahores, an 84-year-old chemistry professor and activist who has mobilised against mega-mining projects for more than two decades, took to the streets in Argentina. Alongside workers, retirees, students, Indigenous groups and human rights organisations, Sahores was there to protest against the country’s far-right president, Javier Milei. During the marcha de la bronca – the “march of anger” – protesters held signs reading, among other rallying cries, “The land is not for sale”.

Marching in Esquel, a town nestled in the foothills of the Andes in Chubut province, she also held up a sign defending the country’s water resources against what she called the government’s “handover” to investors.
